reasoning: Buildability: both are M/stdlib/fixture-pair with identical 5-stage delivery, but lite precommits to strictly less surface — single spine, no --spine/--chain registry, no mini-C2/defender-playbook — making it the likelier to reach full build + green smoke test THIS session on win32; v2's optional spines sit exactly on the completion boundary and compete with the core for the session budget.

Mission fit at M: both cover discover->enumerate->triage->exploit->payload->persist->report through the same core chain; lite keeps the full loop (confidence-formula triage, control-arm FP gate, FE-auth-bypass->admin-RCE, fake-scheduler persist, marker-scoped wipe, report) and needs only the trivial fixture-port discover (implicit in its fixture stage) for step 1.

Dare vs buildability: the harness's optional spines add conceptual breadth but real bloat risk (each adds gate+evidence-writer integration surface), and every folded-in spine was individually judged mission-incomplete; lite cuts nothing mission-critical — cron/systemd, full C2, cache-poison/XSS chains, docker, httpx are all optionality, while the load-bearing dare — objective confidence formula + hard FP_max=0.05 control-arm gate gating weaponization — survives intact in the single blade.

Scope gate: both declare the same canonicalizing resolver + per-probe DNS-rebinding re-resolve + --confirm-lab hard-refuse + lab-UUID marker gating RCE/persist/wipe + loopback-bound listeners; lite's single-spine funnel gives strictly fewer integration points where gate drift could hide.
